findings: Tracker locally held prediction 738 at revocation; its 125 ms observation-validity deadline had elapsed.

Prediction 739 generation started before revocation. Its publication time and Tracker callback order are not recorded. Observer receipt and generation-start time cannot establish availability to Tracker before revocation.
The last two valid observation epochs were separated by about 100 ms, rather than the nominal 50 ms.
Navigation, target, observation, lock, visibility and flight-mode flags were healthy at this event. Lease expiry, geometry validation failure and start missed did not trigger it.
599 R11 source/patch files and both generated flight/research configurations equal this run. 3901 protected paths and 41 historical attempt/summary claims are unchanged.

No observed missing-file/import error or online dependency on archived files. This supports a timing boundary failure with unchanged code; it does not prove the exact DDS/executor/camera scheduling cause.
limits: No full tracker subscription dequeue trace or sensor frame publication log; cannot attribute the missing observation to rendering, bridge, or detector.
Owned CPU load and near-unit RTF do not prove absence of transient process scheduling delays.
Revocation-time and debug-time validity overshoot differ by about 0.26 ms; use revocation epoch for causal expiry claim.

diagnostic_followup.condition: Strict same-source and same-config F2 repeat; F3 only if original gate and predetermined maintenance comparison all pass.
diagnostic_followup.purpose: Determine whether the input timing boundary recurs under an independent identical launch, without changing online code/config/thresholds.

prediction_generation_timestamp_semantic: generated is the time captured at generation start; compute_time is measured before publisher call; it is not a publication/receiver availability timestamp.
